# `prefer-index-of-scalar`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: idiomatic · Default: off · Fixes: fix all · Options: none

Reports `std.mem.find`, `findLast`, `findAny`, `findLastAny`, and `count` calls
with a single-byte string literal.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

Scalar search states that only one element is needed and uses the standard
library's scalar scanning implementation.

## When it fires

It also accepts their legacy `indexOf` spellings. The fix uses `findScalar`,
`findScalarLast`, or `countScalar` with a character literal.

The needle must decode to one byte. Multi-byte strings and calls that already
use scalar search stay unchanged.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
const std = @import("std");

fn hasComma(line: []const u8) bool {
    return std.mem.find(u8, line, ",") != null;
}
```
